local.title: In the City of Trees, owning one comes with duties.
local.intro: Royal Oak has been a Tree City USA for about 50 years, and planting here goes back to the 1930s. A lot of those trees are now big, old and close to something. The city looks after its own on a fixed schedule, and it expects owners to look after theirs.

points.title: The city works on a long cycle
points.body: Street trees get pruned by block. Royal Oak is split into eight sections and aims to finish one a year, so a tree may wait years for its turn. It works from that schedule, not from single requests, and the block trimming map shows when your section comes up.

points.title: Stop at the sidewalk
points.body: The lawn strip along the curb is public right of way. A tree there has to be pruned by the city or under a city permit, so we stay on your side of the walk. A dead street tree or a hanging limb is worth a call to Public Works.

points.title: Your limbs are your job
points.body: If your tree hangs over the street, city code makes it your job. Owners must keep eight feet clear above the road, keep growth off streetlights and out of the view at intersections, and remove dead or dangerous limbs that threaten the public. If our crew can reach it safely, we will take care of it.

points.title: Elms get a yearly check
points.body: Every year the city surveys for Dutch elm disease, private yards included. An infected elm is declared a public nuisance and has to be dealt with within 30 days, at the owner's expense on private land. That clock is short, so call early if yours looks wrong.

points.title: Oaks wait for November
points.body: Oak wilt kills red oaks and can get in through fresh cuts. The Michigan Oak Wilt Coalition puts the greatest risk at April 15 to July 15, and lists November 1 to March 14 as the time to prune without painting cuts. Ask early, and Jake will say whether he can get to your oak in that window or who can.

logistics.title: On a Royal Oak lot, the first question is whose tree it is.
body: Jake walks the tree with you and tells you whose it is and who should do the work. If it is ours, the itemized estimate says what is being cut and what is staying.

Small lots change how a tree comes out. A limb over a garage or a neighbor's fence has to come down in pieces, and a narrow side yard limits what can get through. Anything near a power line is a job for the utility, not for us.

How the brush gets off the lot goes on your estimate. That matters here, because curbside yard waste only takes wood up to 2 inches thick, pieces up to 5 inches go with the trash under the city's brush rules, and anything bigger is on the owner.

faq.q: Do you do tree trimming in Royal Oak?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape trims trees and takes down smaller ones on private property in Royal Oak, and we can [grind the stump](/stump-grinding/) too. Jake hands the big ones to a tree company, including any big ash still standing dead near a house, since emerald ash borer killed thousands of the city's trees years ago. Call or text [(586) 718-8762](tel:+15867188762) for a free estimate.

faq.q: When will Royal Oak trim the street tree in front of my house?
faq.a: When your section comes up. Pruning runs by block across eight sections, with a goal of one section a year, and the city's block trimming map shows the schedule. We do not work on street trees, because all work on a public tree must be done by the city or under a right of way permit from Engineering. A private contractor can pull that permit if you do not want to wait. Call Public Works if the tree is completely dead or a broken branch is hanging.

faq.q: Can I take down a tree on my own lot in Royal Oak without a permit?
faq.a: The city's forestry pages make private trees the owner's responsibility, and the permits they describe are for public trees. Its climate plan also calls for studying an ordinance to protect existing residential trees, so call the city before a big removal to confirm what applies to your lot. Jake will flag anything he notices at the estimate.

faq.q: When should I prune my oak?
faq.a: Between November 1 and mid March, the stretch the Michigan Oak Wilt Coalition treats as clear for trimming oaks without sealing the cuts. Ask Jake early whether he can do it in that stretch or who can. Risk is greatest from April 15 to July 15, and the months on either side are lower but not zero. If a storm breaks an oak between mid March and the end of October, paint the wound right away with shellac or latex paint.

faq.q: What do I do with storm branches in Royal Oak?
faq.a: The city chips branches that fall from public trees. Branches from private trees are yours to deal with. From April to mid December, pieces under 4 feet long and 2 to 5 inches thick can be bundled for trash day, and bigger ones may need a chipping service. If it came off a smaller tree, text a photo to [(586) 718-8762](tel:+15867188762) and we will say whether it is a job for us.
